comparator.name: Religiewetenschappen
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official programme page confirms a 180-EC, 36-month bachelor. The curriculum accounts for all 180 EC. Year one is 60 EC: 36 EC of required Religious Studies courses (Judaism, Christianity, textual analysis, Islam, Hinduism/Buddhism, and lived religion) plus one 24-EC restricted-choice package drawn from first-year courses in History, Art History, Philosophy, Media Studies, Hebrew, Arabic, or European Studies. Year two is 60 EC of ten listed 6-EC Religious Studies components spanning religion/art/culture, Western esotericism, religion and spirituality in the Netherlands, philosophy of science, disciplinary history/philosophy, and two research projects. Year three is 60 EC: Utopias and Future Visions (6), Religion and Popular Culture (6), Bachelor-thesis Research Project (6), genuine free-choice space (30), and the Bachelor Thesis (12). The research project plus thesis form the stated 18-EC graduation trajectory. The optional double-degree and abbreviated two-year route are not part of the reconstructed ordinary bachelor.

exception.reason: The UvA bachelor is defined by sustained disciplinary study of Judaism, Christianity, Islam, Hinduism and Buddhism; sacred-text interpretation; lived religion; Western esotericism; religion and spirituality in the Netherlands; religious art, myth and popular culture; disciplinary history and philosophy; and two dedicated Religious Studies research projects culminating in a thesis. UCR has relevant courses in philosophy, sociology, politics, history, archaeology, literature and cultural analysis, but no course or sequence in Religious Studies, theology, comparative religion, sacred texts, lived religion or the history of religious traditions. A 24-course UCR programme could examine culture, ideas and institutions around religion, yet most courses would treat religion only incidentally and would omit the target’s defining disciplinary core. Publishing it as a closest match would therefore misstate what UCR teaches.
exception.curriculumContext: The current official overview and study-programme page jointly establish a complete ordinary 180-EC pathway. The 24-EC first-year restricted choice and 30-EC later free-choice space are preserved as choices rather than populated with invented content. The optional double-degree and shortened post-propaedeutic route are excluded from the ordinary bachelor reconstruction.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 records in the current GitHub main data/reference/ucr_courses_enriched.xlsx, including names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned availability. GOSPHIL111 Introduction to Western Philosophy, GOSPHIL212 Ethics, GOSSOCI111 Introduction to Sociology, GOSSOCI214 Modern Sociology, GOSPOLI111 Introduction to Political Philosophy, GOSHIST111 Modern History and GOSSOCI212 Qualitative Research Methodology can support historical, philosophical and social-scientific inquiry. MCCHEAM112 Introduction to World Archaeology, MCCHEAM211 African Art & Heritage, MCCHEAM212 Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean, MCCHEAM315 Heritage & Ancient Democracy, MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works and MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature include limited religious, Islamic or mythic material. GOSLAWJ213 Comparative Constitutional Law considers religion only within constitutional questions, and GOSPHIL214 Philosophy of Mind briefly includes Buddhist philosophy. None studies religion as the disciplinary object or provides comparative-religion, sacred-text, ritual, theology, esotericism, lived-religion or Religious Studies research training. These adjacent courses cannot form a substantively honest 24-course closest-match degree.
